author: Deeg
asr_identification: the site N of the citadel of Anurādhapura (Abhayagiri dagoba and monastery), North Central Province, Sri Lanka
evidence: Summarises the archaeological identification: the site north of the citadel and of the Mahāvihāra and Jetavana, with a monumental stūpa (citing Bandaranayake 1974; Coningham 1999: 2), much larger than the Mahāvihāra, its art showing Āndhra influence (Bopearachchi 2020); finds attesting long-distance contacts (Davis 2013). Inscriptions from the northern stūpa of Abhayagiri read by Schopen (1982) as dhāraṇīs of the *Sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānahṛdaya; a Ratu Baka (Java) inscription of 856 links the monastery to Java. None of the inscriptions cited names the site itself.
quote: there is archaeological evidence of the monastery in precincts of the ancient…capital of Anurādhapura. The site identified with the Abhayagirivihāra, north of…the citadel and the other two monasteries, the Mahāvihāra and the Jetavanavihāra,…has a monumental stūpa (Bandaranayake 1974; Coningham 1999: 2)
note: Agrees with the study and Mizutani (Abhayagiri, N of Anurādhapura, medium). Reports the received identification and the site's monuments and dhāraṇī inscriptions; cites no inscription at the site naming Abhayagiri, so the grade is unchanged.

author: Deeg
asr_identification: the great stūpa N of the royal city = the Abhayagiri stūpa, Anurādhapura
evidence: Reads Faxian (T.2085.864c): a great stūpa 40 zhang high built over the Buddha's footprint N of the royal city, with the monastery Wuwei-shan (Abhayagiri, 5,000 monks) beside it. Deeg matches Faxian's height (over 90 m, at c. 2.3 m to the zhang) to the size of the Abhayagiri stūpa, so that Faxian's description refers to that monument, and suggests the Abhayagiri's lost foundation legend placed a footprint under it.
quote: A king had a large stūpa erected on…top of the footstep in the north of the city, forty zhang97 high…A comparison between the…size of the Abhayagiri stūpa and the measure – a height of over 90 m – given by…Faxian shows that the monk’s description indeed refers to this stūpa.
note: Agrees. Ties Faxian's 5th-c. Abhayagiri to the surviving stūpa N of the city (a matching monument for Faxian's account, not for Xuanzang, who gives no site); the study's site stands. Xuanzang's own entry is hearsay and names a fraternity, so medium stays.

author: Deeg
name_in_asr: 摩訶毘訶羅住部 Mohepiheluo-zhu-bu (Mahāvihāravāsin); 阿跋耶祇釐住部 Abayeqili-zhu-bu (Abhayagirivāsin)
asr_identification: the two fraternities of the Mahāvihāra and the Abhayagiri, Anurādhapura (no site argued)
evidence: Translates T.2087.934a.14–19 and reconstructs the names: -zhu 住 renders -vāsin, so Xuanzang names the two communities (Mahāvihāra-dwellers, Abhayagiri-dwellers), not the buildings. He reads the account as from Abhayagiri informants: the Life's Sri Lankan monks met at Kāñcīpura (Bodhimegheśvara, Abhayadaṃṣṭra, over 300 monks, c. 637) were probably Abhayagiri monks and Xuanzang's main source.
quote: Mohepiheluo(-zhu-bu) 摩訶毘訶羅(住部)…-zhu 住 obviously translates…the Skt. ending -vāsin (Mahāvihāravāsin)…Abayeqili(-zhu-bu) 阿跋耶祇釐(住部)
note: Agrees with the identifications (Mahāvihāra and Abhayagiri, medium) and sharpens the reading: the Xiyu ji names the two nikāyas by their -vāsin names and gives no location; the sites rest on the vaṃsas, Faxian and the monuments, not on Xuanzang. Hearsay, probably from Abhayagiri monks at Kāñcī.

author: Deeg
evidence: Dates Xuanzang's abandoned visit to c. 637, under Aggabodhi III Sirimeghavaṇṇa; the famine and the king's death reported in the Life are not in the Cūḷavaṃsa. No bearing on location.
quote: When looking at the account of the events in the Cūḷavaṃsa at the time of…Xuanzang’s attempt to visit the island, probably around 637, then this time…can be identified with the rule of king Aggabodhi III Sirimeghavaṇṇa
note: No bearing on the identification (Sri Lanka, capital Anurādhapura). Confirms the entry is hearsay.
